source.title: COMPUTE-MFG-001C: PCB fabrication, assembly, rework, and test capability profile
source.body:
Parent: [COMPUTE-MFG-001 #5796](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5796). Compose [MFG-PROC-000 #5686](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5686), [MFG-PROC-001 #5688](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5688), [HMI-MFG-001B #5799](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5799), [SEMI-ROADMAP-001 #5867](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5867), existing fabrication authority and evidence/metrology owners, plus [AtomFab PCB productive-closure roadmap PR #8222](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/8222).

## Purpose

Freeze the first executable, evidence-bounded benchmark for designing, routing, fabricating or sourcing, assembling, inspecting, repairing, and testing a small low-voltage PCB.

This is the PCB-specific implementation slice of the existing computer/electronics closure program. It does not create a parallel process ontology, BOM authority, inspection ledger, capability-closure engine, or machine-control path.

## Core distinctions

~~~text
PCB design exists != design passes declared DRC/DFM
Gerber/drill export exists != bare board has been fabricated
bare board passes inspection != assembly is functional
local assembly != local bare-board production
local bare-board production != local IC/passive/connector manufacture
chip RTL/design != fabricated, packaged, tested silicon
~~~

## First article profile

Use a repairable low-voltage 2-layer sensor/controller board or wired macropad, selected and frozen after a design-for-manufacture review. Keep the first article outside mains voltage, high-energy power conversion, and safety-critical control.

Track independently: native design and library dependencies; electrical netlist; BOM / substitutes; manufacturing output bundle; bare-board route; assembly recipe; as-built identity; firmware identity; required inspection and electrical/functional test evidence; repair/rework history.

## Route profiles to compare

- **P0: outsourced bare board + local assembly/test.** Supplier service and lot are explicit external dependencies.
- **P1: local isolation milling/drilling + local assembly/test.** Admissible only for feature requirements actually supported by the exact machine/material/tool/fixture profile; do not assume plated-through vias, industrial solder mask/finish, multilayer, impedance control, or high-density capability.
- **P2: image/etch prototype route.** Representation only unless separately reviewed site/process safety and waste-management profiles are present; this issue gives no chemical recipe or operating setpoint.
- **P3: conventional multilayer route.** Keep as an external qualified supplier profile initially; model internal lamination, drilling, desmear/plating, mask/finish, and electrical-test capability only as separate future qualification stages.

## Synthetic corpus

Freeze at least 16 small known-answer cases before implementing route selection. Include positive controls and negative controls for:

1. valid P0 route with supplier capability evidence and complete output bundle;
2. valid simple P1 route with no plated vias;
3. P1 requested for plated-through vias;
4. P1 requested for multilayer stack-up;
5. route's minimum trace/space capability unknown;
6. missing or stale DRC/DFM evidence;
7. missing or revision-mismatched drill output;
8. required solder mask or surface finish unavailable in selected route;
9. unapproved component substitution changes a protected BOM requirement;
10. missing required bare-board inspection;
11. stale/missing calibration for a measurement used for acceptance;
12. missing assembly/placement artifact;
13. solder/placement inspection incomplete for the product profile;
14. functional tests use wrong firmware or board revision;
15. missing lot/as-built provenance;
16. synthetic or supplier-declared results incorrectly promoted as independent physical qualification.

The independent oracle must derive dispositions from profile/case relationships, not echo expected output fields. Include duplicate IDs, wrong schema, altered case count, mismatched digests and missing negative controls as corpus-integrity attacks.

## Acceptance and metrics

- 100% agreement with independently derived known-answer dispositions.
- 100% rejection of the registered invalid routes; all unresolved prerequisites return **incomplete** or **reject**, never silent pass.
- Process feasibility, board quality, assembly quality, functional results, cost, lead time, resource impact, repairability and import dependence stay as separate outputs; no scalar score can override a hard gate.
- Every route and receipt binds exact design revision, netlist/BOM, route/capability profile, schema/corpus digest, tool versions and Git HEAD.
- Input order does not change canonical identity; a material, netlist, recipe, profile or protected-datum change changes the appropriate subject identity.
- Physical targets for trace/space, drill accuracy, yield and reliability are defined from the actual article/product class and measured with suitable instruments; do not infer them from commanded step size or simulation.
- Cost per accepted board includes labour, setup, consumables, tool wear, depreciation, utilities, inspection, scrap, rework and external supplier charges; disclose sample size and uncertainty.

## Implementation sequence

1. Freeze the schema / fixture contract and independent oracle.
2. Add deterministic Rust validation and a reproducible receipt; run locally before relying on hosted CI.
3. Add a KiCad CLI export / package-inventory adapter behind the existing process contract; never execute machine outputs from untrusted or unvalidated design input.
4. Connect to the existing fabrication gateway only for already-qualified, explicitly authorized process profiles.
5. Add as-built, netlist, inspection, functional-test and repair evidence composition.
6. Extend to SMT automation / OpenPnP only after the first article and its manual baseline are reproducible.

## Non-goals

No machine actuation or new execution authority; no hazardous process recipes; no claim of multilayer production qualification; no claim of locally fabricated semiconductors; no claim that passing synthetic cases establishes physical yields or reliability.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: Implementation update in [AtomFab PR #8222](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/8222): the v0.2 corpus now cleanly separates route feasibility from evidence completeness and records multiple gate failures independently. Added `atomfab_pcb_route` Rust evaluator, SHA-256 corpus receipt, exact Git-head requirement, CLI runner and unit tests for independent oracle agreement, duplicate IDs/count tampering, changed expected result, order normalization and synthetic-evidence overclaim. The tests are added but have not been run in this work session; commit status currently has no reported status contexts. Next implementation step remains real KiCad output/package binding and then physical evidence composition, behind existing process and fabrication authority contracts.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: Further hardening in [AtomFab PR #8222](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/8222): the corpus is now v0.3, and the CLI runs `git rev-parse HEAD` and refuses to emit a receipt if `ATOMFAB_GIT_HEAD` doesn't match the checked-out commit. A second negative control changes the evidence-source label to `measured` and still must reject physical qualification; the corpus does not include actual measured data or calibration artifacts. These are code/test additions, not yet a reported Rust test pass or physical-process qualification.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: Exact-head focused validation is now **passing** on the updated AtomFab PR head `a275bcb0311b6c70750bb5488b1f9af4d5022b3c`: [AtomFab PCB Route Corpus workflow #39486713433](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/actions/runs/39486713433). It passed exact-source rustfmt, the isolated Rust unit tests, route/evidence oracle checks, exact-head receipt generation, byte-identical replay, and the wrong-Git-SHA negative control. Receipt artifact digest: `sha256:9f0228d1b0962ee8821cd7088a0acd6c1a73fbe992c47e1d718a47d3026d3c8f9`. This does not clear the separate whole-workspace manifest blocker tracked in #7048/#6971 and does not establish physical PCB qualification.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: Next tranche added on the AtomFab branch: a 12-case synthetic PCB manufacturing-package integrity corpus and Rust validator. It checks binding between native board/schematic sources, netlist/BOM, DRC source digest/profile/revision, Gerber/drill/outline exports, BOM and placement artifacts; it rejects missing roles, stale revision/digests, duplicate paths, directory traversal, DRC violations, and unknown DRC status. `ready_for_review` is explicitly not manufacturing approval or execution authority. The route evaluator's focused green run is still valid at its exact tested head; the expanded route+package workflow on the newer package-code head has been triggered, but I am not claiming that code as passing yet.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
## Actual-byte artifact inventory extension (2026-10-21)

Work is now being added in [AtomFab PR #8222](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/8222) as `atomfab_pcb_artifacts` plus an exact-HEAD-bound example receipt runner. Compared with the package-manifest consistency gate, this evaluator reads files beneath a canonical artifact root and computes SHA-256 from the bytes actually present; it rejects unsafe paths, root-escaping symlinks, duplicate/undeclared roles, and expected-digest mismatches, and reports `complete` / `incomplete` / `rejected`.

The smoke fixture files are labelled synthetic placeholders; this is not a native KiCad design, real DRC output, Gerber, or physical evidence. The latest focused workflow on commit `f4c9d24ad7480da63678a619fb0b478a96b74b52` is queued after fixing the formatter findings; I am not claiming the new tests pass yet.

Next physical-design bridge: add a small frozen native KiCad project and run a pinned `kicad-cli` toolchain in CI for DRC plus Gerber/drill export. Keep clean/violated design controls, pin tool version and command/exit status, hash output bytes, parse the DRC report, and keep the release gate false unless all separate capability, review, and physical-qualification evidence exists. The current inventory gate itself must never imply DRC cleanliness or production readiness.
